To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the topological symmetries of large interconnection networks can be used in conjunction with the algebraic specification of permutation voltage graphs in order to facilitate algebraic specification of guest-host network relationships.

a mapping between two base graphs is liftable to a mapping between the respective coverings if and only if the base graphs have isomorphic permutation voltage graphs, and that the lift is uniquely determined by the mapping and by the permutation voltage graphs.

the algebraic specification of a network relationship is facilitated by permutation voltage graph coverings and that the algebraic properties of a network relationship are reflected in the algebraic structure of the corresponding graph coverings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of algebraic methods for the specification of interconnection networks.

the algebraic specification of network relationships, in particular of guest-host network relationships, in which symmetries of large graphs are exploited to simplify the specification process and the resulting specification is used to facilitate the design of efficient guest-host mappings.
algebraically specified interconnection network relationships, with the symmetries of the networks involved, and with the algebraic properties of the mappings that are intended between the networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the new approach provides a new and powerful tool for specifying and for understanding the structure of interconnection networks. (This paper is a revised version of a paper that was presented at the IEEE 2005 Symposium on Application-Specific Processors.)
algebraic specification of guest-host relationships is a viable alternative to the more traditional specification of guest-host mappings in terms of graph isomorphisms.
algebraic specification of interconnections by permutation voltage graphs can be made to yield the most general and most efficient specification of guest-host network relationships.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a method for algebraically specifying a mapping of a graph into a larger graph, with the smaller graph being the guest and the larger being the host, and with the host having a symmetry property that it is algebraic and isomorphic to a covering graph.

we have developed a new approach to network design that uses algebraic topology to specify a network relationship between two graphs, and then applies the theory of permutation voltage graphs to lift this relationship topologically to a larger guest-host pair of graphs.
we have developed an algebraic theory of graph coverings that facilitates the specification and analysis of interconnection network mappings.
The main takeaway from our work is that

algebraic specification is not merely a matter of convenience for the sake of simplifying a specification, but that it also has a profound influence on the structure of the resulting guest-host network relationship, and that this influence can be understood in terms of a mathematical theory of symmetries of graphs.
the algebraic specification of a guest or a host network is an effective means of specifying the network topology of a large-scale network.
the symmetries of a network are a powerful tool for simplifying algebraic specification of guest-host relationships.
